page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr9i.36xlarge is an enterprise instance within the High Clock Speed family, designed for workloads requiring a balance of massive multi-threaded parallel execution and dense system memory. The virtual machine runs on KVM virtualization using the x86_64 architecture and provides 144 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at a sustained base frequency of 3.4 GHz. With all cores dedicated, the instance avoids resource contention typical of shared compute platforms.

System memory capacity is sized at 1536.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of approximately 10.67 GB of RAM per vCPU. Networking interfaces provide a baseline throughput of 64 Gbps, facilitating high-bandwidth interconnects and external storage transfers. The instance includes no local storage volumes and no discrete hardware accelerators, meaning persistent and scratch data must be provisioned via remote cloud storage services.

Given the high memory-to-core allocation paired with a 3.4 GHz clock rate, the server delivers strong resource density for demanding enterprise platforms. It is particularly well suited for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large enterprise resource planning systems, data warehousing, and memory-bound computational pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr9i.36xlarge is a high-clock-speed, memory-dense instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. It is provisioned with 144 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at 3.4 GHz, paired with 1536.0 GB of system memory, providing an extensive 10.67 GB per vCPU. The configuration contains no discrete graphics hardware and provides no onboard local storage, relying on external network-attached volumes backed by a 64 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. By combining elevated processor clock rates with an exceptionally large memory pool, this instance type efficiently accommodates large memory footprints without sacrificing per-core throughput. It is technically suited for scale-up in-memory databases, massive SAP/ERP deployments, high-throughput computational analytics, and distributed in-memory data processing.
